subject: Request: evidence for onshore processing + retention-exception and DPA addendum (Arcadia Health)
messages:
From: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence for onshore processing + retention-exception and DPA addendum (Arcadia Health)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Arcadia is excited about Redwood for clinical note summarization. Before we proceed to procurement, our legal and privacy teams need to close three items for our internal risk committee:

1) Evidence that processing for the Arcadia tenant can be restricted to onshore infrastructure (US-only) and a short certificate or attestation for the same.
2) A retention-exception confirmation for a subset of PII derived outputs (we retain patient-identified transcripts for 90 days, but regulator counsel prefers an exception for 180 days for ongoing clinical review). We need to understand how that exception will be documented in the DPA (and whether an amendment is needed).
3) Excerpt from your Article 30 processing register and any DPIA support you can provide that maps to clinical data flows.

Can you confirm what evidence you can provide, an expected timeline, and whether you can accept/execute a DPA addendum (we have a standard addendum attached to this email for reference).

Attachment: Arcadia_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf (PDF, 280 KB)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — the committee meets on Friday.

Best,
Clara Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Arcadia Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for onshore processing + retention-exception and DPA addendum (Arcadia Health)

Clara — thanks for the note and the addendum. We can support all three asks but want to align on a compact plan so you have what the committee needs by Friday. Quick summary and proposed timeline: 

- Onshore processing evidence: we can provide a signed on-prem/region attestation and an excerpt of the instance config showing US-only regions (deliverable: onshore_processing_certificate_snippet.pdf). Target: EOD Wednesday.
- Retention-exception: we will propose a DPA addendum clause that explicitly permits a 180-day retention window for the specific derived PII outputs you described, scoped to Arcadia tenant data. I'll draft a redline and loop in Legal (marissa_cole) for sign-off. Target: first draft Wednesday morning.
- Article 30 + DPIA support: we can provide a CSV excerpt of our Article 30 register focused on processor activities and a short DPIA mapping doc that highlights where model inference, caching, and logs fit in the data flow. Attachment: redwood_art30_register_excerpt.csv. ETA: Thursday.

Could you confirm the exact data types subject to the exception (e.g., clinician audio, transcription text, derived notes) and whether the 180-day window applies to backups/exports as well? That detail will determine the language in the addendum.

If it's helpful, we'll provision a restricted Drive folder (link below) for the evidence artifacts and we can do a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk your privacy team through the Art.30 excerpt.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedLink

Thanks — I'll start the redline and loop Legal.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for onshore processing + retention-exception and DPA addendum (Arcadia Health)

Hi Clara — looping in a couple of specifics from the DPIA/support side.

We can provide the following artifacts into the secure folder:
- Article 30 excerpt (processor activities): redwood_art30_register_excerpt.csv (attached).
- Short DPIA mapping (2 pages) that maps risk mitigations for clinical text inference to the Arcadia data categories.
- Onshore processing certificate (snippet) signed by our infrastructure team: onshore_processing_certificate_snippet.pdf.

Clarifying Qs that will change the addendum language:
- Please confirm whether "derived notes" include any pseudonymized identifiers (we treat pseudonymized joins as processing that may be reversible only with customer keys).
- Will Arcadia accept scoped language that excludes long-term backups from the 180-day exception (we can include backups only if you confirm a retention schedule for archived backups)?

Attachment: redwood_art30_register_excerpt.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

If you confirm the two bullets above I will work with Karthik to produce a tight addendum clause that Marissa can review. Happy to jump on a quick call at 11:00 PT if you prefer.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Privacy Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Torres <ben.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 07:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for onshore processing + retention-exception and DPA addendum (Arcadia Health)

Karthik / Lauren — quick answers from our side after an internal check:

- Derived notes = clinician audio transcriptions + any machine-generated summary text. We do not plan to include pseudonymized joins in the derived note set (those are out of scope).
- Backups: Arcadia prefers to exclude backups from the 180-day exception. Archives/backups must remain at 90 days unless we supply a separate justification to regulator counsel.

I've uploaded our data mapping worksheet to the folder for your reference (Attachment: Arcadia_Data_Map.xlsx). Also, Clara sent a standard DocuSign envelope for the addendum (link below). We're OK with Redwood proposing redline language; we plan to have counsel review and sign within 24 hours after we receive the redline.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/recipient-status?envelopeId=0a1b2c3d4e5f

Thanks — Ben
Director, Procurement
Arcadia Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood redline: DPA addendum + evidence folder ready

Marissa / team — attaching my proposed redline to Arcadia's addendum to capture the 180-day exception scoping (derived notes only) and the explicit exclusion of backups from that exception. Key points in the redline:

- Defined scope: "Derived notes" = clinician audio transcriptions and machine-generated summaries; expressly excludes any datasets that contain reversible pseudonymization or joins requiring Arcadia keys.
- Retention clause: "Notwithstanding Section X of the DPA, Processor may retain Derived Notes for a period not to exceed 180 days for the purpose of clinical review, with backups and archives excluded unless separately agreed in writing."
- Article 28/30 evidence: we will drop the Article 30 excerpt and onshore certificate into the shared folder.
- Operational controls: added a short paragraph on tenant-level encryption and KMS key ownership.

Attachment: karthik_dpa_addendum_redline.docx (DOCX, 36 KB)
Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedLink

Clara / Ben — please review the redline in the Drive folder. If the language looks good we will ask Marissa to countersign and route the DocuSign envelope back to you. Target: countersign by tomorrow EOD.

Karthik
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
